newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, eye on payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, eye on payrolls data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in active trade on Thursday, helped by tame U.S. GDP and inflation data and a lack of selling by domestic accounts at month's end.

"In Canada we had the GDP number, which came in as expected, so it was a relief, but I think the key thing was the U.S. number," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.38 to C$122.71 to yield 6.301 percent, a record low yield for the 30-year benchmark.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 10/32 to yield 6.31 percent. The spread between the bonds was unchanged from Wednesday's close at negative one basis point.

Bonds in both countries rallied after the U.S. Commerce Department said on Thursday that GDP grew at a 2.2 percent annual rate in the second quarter, down from a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter.
Analysts said the downward revision and the tame implicit price deflator, a key measure of inflation, were bullish for fixed-income markets in both countries.
Bond investors are now awaiting the key U.S. employment data for July due out on Friday. Dealers said many accounts were neutrally positioned ahead of the report.

"Most accounts are very reluctant to sell any securities going into month end, especially with non-farm payrolls coming out in the U.S. tomorrow," said one institutional bond salesman at a bank-owned brokerage. "To me the highlight of the market is the total absence of any selling pressure.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it planned to auction on August 6 C$2.3 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon maturing on June 1, 2008.

The Bank of Canada will buy at least C$345 million of the new bonds. The bonds, which will be dated and delivered on August 15, pay interest on June 1 and December 1, the government said. No bonds mature on August 15, 1997.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.14 to C$110.84 to yield 5.786 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.02 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 23 basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
